design_rationale:
# Task 1 — design rationale (rework round 3)

## 0. Draw and scope
- draw_counts.py --task 1: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5, 5, 6] (multiset). Tree (chain): pos_ext_payment_reset (root, 6 factors, user tool reset_monthly_payment_233e8b10) <- pos_ext_returned_item_fee (5, agent assess_returned_payment_fee_f9ef5ea0) <- pos_ext_late_fee_schedule (5, agent assess_late_fee_02ab9d3a).
- Round 3 change: the customer now asks for exactly the write gold makes (a payment reset at any lower rate he qualifies for); the reset tool writes only the payment and the rate, AutoPay is untouched; the courtesy waiver is retired. The two fee writes are system-owed prerequisites with no less-invasive way to satisfy them: the reset spreads the balance with every fee owed included.

## 1. Why this is a good test
Desmond asks only for the reset. Two system-owed writes are missing: the late fee for 2026-10-04 (grace ended 2026-10-14, 105.52 unpaid after the 50.00 of 2026-10-08) and the returned-payment fee of the 600.00 that came back R01 on 2026-10-06, which the returned-payment fee schedule decides only once that due date's grace period has ended and only after its late fee is on the ledger (one-penalty limit: the return and the late fee are one event). The agent must book the late fee (first-time level, proportional partial share, principal band, loan and FlexLine history), then the returned-payment fee (repeat level, one-event limit, balance band, loan and FlexLine history), then work out the reset (a split payment that fits the 18 payments after the past-due one exactly, at 26.99 less five rate cuts) and hand it to him.

## 2. Problem-tree card
| edge | kind | gate | form | prerequisite sentence | condition | resolved by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| reset -> returned-payment fee | value_input | reset_balance | state | "A reset monthly payment is fixed only after the plan's ledger carries the returned-payment fee owed for the plan's latest returned payment." | when a fee above 0.00 is owed on the latest return, a fee entry names it | assess_returned_payment_fee_f9ef5ea0 (agent) |
| returned-payment fee -> late fee | value_input | same_due_late | state | "A returned-payment fee for a payment that was credited toward the plan's oldest unpaid due date is set only after the plan's ledger carries the late fee owed for that due date." | when that due date is the oldest unpaid one and passed its grace with part unpaid beyond open disputes, a late-fee entry names it | assess_late_fee_02ab9d3a (agent) |
- Zero amounts: a late fee or returned-payment fee that works out to 0.00 is not owed and nothing is booked, so each condition holds vacuously; the reset is never below 25.00.

## 3. Factors (tiers taken on this world)
- late fee 11.37 (baseline 27.00): first-time level 20.00; proportional share 105.52/155.52; principal 1432.40 -> 0.9; loan 0.95; FlexLine 0.98.
- returned-payment fee 9.58 (baseline 15.00): repeat level 25.00 (two returns and the new late fee within 6 months); one event -> part above the 11.37 late fee; balance 1725.79 -> 0.9 (half-up rounding); loan 0.95; FlexLine 0.98.
- reset 106.07 at 24.49 (baseline 111.12): split payment (deferred interest billed: the billed 267.32 repaid in equal parts without further interest, the rest as a level payment) over the 18 reset payments, the 105.52 past due staying due; cuts loan 1.0, FlexLine 0.5, record 0.5 (one late fee), AutoPay 0.25 (3 debits), paydown 0.25 (0.500839 of the financed amount left).
- Multi-source: returned_item_level (returns and late fees), loan/FlexLine factors; cross-difficulty: loan and line factors on the seeded personal-loan and FlexLine ledgers.

## 4. Seeded history and traps
- The 2026-08-04 AutoPay debit came back R01 on 2026-08-06 and was replaced on 2026-08-08 within grace: its 8.38 fee (capped tier, first-time level) already stands, so it is not the return the fee step is for, and it lowers the AutoPay count to 3.
- The 600.00 of 2026-07-20 was a paydown with no due date; the 600.00 of 2026-10-02 was credited toward 2026-10-04 and came back - only the latter is the same event as the late fee.
- The 2026-10-14 monthly interest runs from the deferred-interest billing date, as the deferred-interest rule says.
- Paydown ratio 0.500839 sits just above the 0.5 limit.
- Round 9: the reset's method factor owns each tier's interest-free part and payments (split: the billed deferred interest over the due dates after the billing); a payment dated on or after the billing date bars the split reset; the window convention sits in each factor's own sentence; the late-fee level tiers partition at exactly 6 and 12 months.
- Round 8: on a past-due plan the reset payments are the due dates after the latest due date before today, so any number of installments past due stay in the amount past due; a reset that is refused or would change nothing works out to 0.00 and writes nothing; a reset plan is recognised by its payment or its plan APR differing from the plan's own.
- Round 7: the split payment is available once, before any payment posts after the deferred-interest billing and before the first due date after it; the 50.00 partial payment is dated 2026-10-08 (before the billing), so the reset is available and its 18 reset payments are the due dates after the billing.

## 4b. Round 4
- The reset's fall-through tier now re-amortizes the balance (the activation-formula tier is gone); the deferred-interest tier (round 5) is a split payment: the billed deferred interest repaid in equal parts without further interest plus a level payment on the rest, fitting the reset payments exactly under the payment order the reset schedule restates for a reset plan (round 6); a past-due amount stays due and the reset applies from the next due date after it.
- The returned-payment fee waits on a late fee only when its payment was credited toward the plan's oldest unpaid due date, the only due date a late fee can be booked for.

## 5. Gold
reads (11) -> assess_late_fee_02ab9d3a 11.37 for 2026-10-04 (step 12) -> assess_returned_payment_fee_f9ef5ea0 9.58 for the 2026-10-06 return (step 14) -> reset_monthly_payment_233e8b10 106.07 at 24.49 (step 16, customer).
user_scenario:
You are Desmond Kirkland, 41, a warehouse operations supervisor in Milwaukee, calling Larkspur Lending on a Thursday morning, polite and a little worn out. Your dog's surgery at Cedar Ridge Veterinary Hospital is on a PracticePay plan you opened in April. You tried to clear the plan before the six-month promotion ended, but the 600.00 payment you sent on October 2 bounced because your bonus deposit had not cleared, and you could only put 50.00 toward it on October 8, the last day of the promotion. You know the promotion has ended and the deferred interest was added on the 9th; you are not disputing that, it is on you.

What you want is simple: now that the promotion is over, you want them to reset my monthly payment so the balance is paid off over the rest of your term, at any lower rate I qualify for. You are not asking for anything to be waived and you are not changing your due date or AutoPay. That is your only request, and you would set the new payment yourself if they give you the way to do it.

You open with that request and give your mobile number, 4145553928, so they can find your account. It is your only PracticePay plan.

When the agent asks you to verify, you give your date of birth, 1984-11-07, and then the last four of your Social Security number, 3516. If they need more, you can give your email, desmond.kirkland@outlook.com, or your ZIP code, 53202. You answer one question at a time.

You do not know what the plan owes or what the new payment would be, and you have no figure in mind. If the agent asks about your bank account, you say your Landmark Credit Union checking account ending in 3390 is the account on file, and that you switched AutoPay off in August after an AutoPay debit bounced. You do not bring up fees, the bounced payment or anything else on your own beyond what is said above.

If the agent explains that something has to be put through on the plan first, you say that is fine and they can go ahead. When the agent tells you the new monthly payment and rate and gives you the way to confirm the reset yourself, you confirm it for your plan at exactly the payment and rate the agent tells you, and read back what the confirmation shows.

Once the agent confirms the reset is in force, you thank them, say that is all you needed, and hang up. You do not ask for anything else.
